title: Stopping signs 2: ج, ۖ, ۗ and the paired three dots: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: At-Tariq 9 to 17, Al-Burooj 1 to 11 and stopping signs
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 34 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Stopping signs 2 rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 34. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Signs that give a choice
points: ج (ۚ): stopping and continuing are equal
∴ ∴ (ۛ, paired dots): stop at one of the two, not both

arabic.text: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيْبَ ۛ فِيهِ ۛ هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ (٢)

keywords.def: stopping on a word, with a breath
a small mark above the line that tells us how to stop
paired dots: stop at one, not both

questions.q: Read 2:2 twice: first stopping at «رَيْبَ», then at «فِيهِ».
questions.a: dhaalikal-kitaabu laa rayb (stop) feehi hudal-lil-muttaqeen; or ... laa rayba feeh (stop) hudal-lil-muttaqeen.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: label eight signs from Juz' 'Amma and Al-Baqarah 2:285 to 286. Today's rota group recites At-Tariq 1 to 17.
questions.a: Each sign labelled with its meaning.

questions.q: Extend: find the ج sign in Al-Fajr 89:23.
Stretch: why is stopping at both paired dots not allowed?
questions.a: The phrase between them would be cut off from both sides and the meaning would break.

questions.q: At the paired dots (ۛ ... ۛ) we may stop at ...
questions.a: A) one of them, not both. Mu'anaqah: stop at one only.

questions.q: Think again: Some signs say 'you choose'. If you have a choice, how do you decide whether to stop?
questions.a: Think about your breath and the meaning: stop only where the meaning stays clear, and start again sensibly.
